sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time (UTC): 2026-10-23 00:24 UTC. Scope: Daily. Date range: 2026-10-23 through 2026-10-23. Ranking basis: daily GitHub Trending star gains, plus one supplemental recent-activity result.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Coding-agent workflows dominate the strongest daily signals: Cloudflare’s security-audit skill leads at +2,979 stars, followed by Ponytail (+1,948) and Graphify (+1,408). The page also shows demand for role-specific AI plugins alongside established developer platforms and core projects.

sections.title: Graphify-Labs/graphify
sections.description: Builds a queryable knowledge graph from a codebase and related documents for coding assistants.
sections.content: Uses local AST parsing for code and labels graph relationships as extracted or inferred; exposes query, path, and explain workflows.
sections.why_notable: Third-highest gain; its local, AST-based code mapping and explicit extracted-versus-inferred graph edges target agent context and code understanding.
sections.unique_caveat: README distinguishes local deterministic code parsing from semantic processing of non-code inputs, which may use a model/backend.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Coding-agent workflows and skills: Cloudflare's audit skill, Ponytail, Anthropic's role plugins, and claude-howto package procedures or domain context around agents. Codebase context and platform infrastructure: Graphify builds a graph for code understanding; Supabase and FastAPI represent application-backend foundations, while CUA adds sandboxed computer-use infrastructure. Core projects and non-AI utilities: php-src and PCL represent runtime and gaming tooling. Languages: Python 4; JavaScript 2; C, TypeScript, Rust, and Visual Basic .NET 1 each.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's clearest pattern is operationalizing AI coding: skills, review/audit routines, team plugins, and codebase memory are attracting the biggest gains. The remaining entries show that this activity sits alongside durable backend and language ecosystems, with computer-use infrastructure emerging as a related but separately sourced signal. Daily star gains are a short-window measure, not evidence of sustained adoption or project quality.
